findings.finding: Bottom-up from the company's own pre-release and guidance: oil realised $85.91 vs $96.78 in Q2 (about -$0.70B pre-tax at ~66 MMbbl/quarter), domestic gas $1.61 vs -$1.48 in Q2 (about +$0.3B on the slide-22 sensitivity), collar loss $94M vs $156M, oil mix 48.8% vs 50.1% guided, and midstream guided at -$100M to +$100M vs $961M adjusted in Q2. Together they imply Q3 adjusted EPS of roughly $1.30-1.50 against a $1.42-1.45 consensus. Nothing in the pre-released lines decides a beat or a miss; the midstream line is the swing (+/-$100M is about +/-$0.07/share).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: OXY beat EPS consensus in each of the last five quarters (+31% Q2 2026, +77% Q1 2026, +94% Q4 2025, +26% Q3 2025, +30% Q2 2025 per optionsanalysissuite), and the stock closed up after each (+4.1% after Q2 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: The inputs were public on Oct 13 and consensus was updated afterwards ($1.42 on Oct 16), so this is mostly priced. If the market expected a decided beat or miss, the consensus would sit visibly away from what the company's own guide arithmetic gives; it does not.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 slide deck (guidance and sensitivities, https://www.oxy.com/siteassets/documents/investors/quarterly-earnings/oxy2q26conferencecallslides.pdf) with the midstream and GoA findings. Two estimate sources give the bar.

findings.finding: Gulf of America net volumes were 110 Mboed in Q3 against a Q3 guide of 115-123 and a FY26 guide of 132-136 (Q2 actual 144). As of Oct 13 they were only 'partially restored', with the rest waiting on a third-party gas pipeline constraint that has no stated end date. A Q4 or FY GoA guide cut on OXY's highest-margin oil barrels is likely, which pressures the Q4 production guide while Q4 crude prices are well above Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior GoA curtailments (Q2 2025, third-party constraints) were absorbed without a large move; no sourced reaction attaches to a GoA guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 volume is public, but the size of the Q4 carry-over is not. No source found by Nov 9 says the constraint was resolved, and the FY GoA guide (132-136) has not been restated. If the market had priced a cut, previews would quote a lowered Q4 GoA number; none was found.
findings.independence: Guidance ranges come from the Q2 slides (slide 13), a different document. Secondary coverage (https://energynewsbeat.co/big-oil-companies/occidentals-big-tease-sets-the-stage-for-earnings/) repeats the 8-K and adds nothing independent.

findings.finding: Q3 midstream is guided at -$100M to +$100M (midpoint 0, down from $961M adjusted in Q2). Two inputs lean toward the top of that range. First, the physical midstream / Al Hosn line beat its Q2 guide on sulfur pricing, and Gulf sulfur set new records into Q3 (KPC July $950/t fob vs $805 in June; Tampa Q3 molten contract a record $705/lt). Second, OXY's total midstream beat the Q2 guide midpoint (~$450M) by about $500M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: midstream $961M vs guide (record since 2018), EPS beat 25-31%, stock +4.1% the next day (https://boereport.com/2026/08/07/occidental-sees-flat-spending-output-in-2027-keeps-focus-on-debt-reduction/amp/).
findings.why_not_priced: Al Hosn sulfur is a small, unmodelled sub-line of a segment guided at a wide range around zero, and consensus has no separate midstream line. If it were priced, consensus would sit near the company's own arithmetic plus a midstream beat ($1.50+); it sits at $1.42-1.45. Offsetting risks: Hormuz disruption to exports (Q2 international -3 Mboed on 'Middle East disruptions') and guided negative crude-export timing.
findings.independence: The slide-25 midstream reconciliation (https://www.oxy.com/siteassets/documents/investors/quarterly-earnings/oxy2q26conferencecallslides.pdf) attributes the Q2 physical-midstream beat to 'higher sulfur pricing at Al Hosn'. The sulfur price is a proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: Domestic lease operating cost was $8.54/boe in Q3 against a Q3 guide of $8.75. Over ~1.2 Mboed of US volume that is roughly $20-25M of pre-tax cost below guide, supporting the 2026 cost-savings narrative.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after OXY last spoke beat Q3 EPS and were sold: Diamondback beat ($5.86 vs $4.92-5.60) and fell from $200.20 to $195.16, then to about $182.7 by Nov 5, on rising 2027 capital at $100 oil and flat oil volumes. Devon beat ($1.42 vs $1.34), stepped up buybacks, and traded down about 2.6%. That is a sector reaction function that sells beats this week and punishes higher 2027 capital, and OXY has already said 2027 capital 'starts at' $5.9B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: OXY itself has not sold its recent beats (five straight up days), so this cuts against its own history; see the next finding.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer prints are known, but the read-across to OXY's 2027 framework is an inference. If OXY's 2027 capital were expected above $5.9B, its own previews would say so; none found.
findings.independence: Devon: https://www.quiverquant.com/news/DEVON+ENERGY+%28%24DVN%29+Releases+Q3+2026+Earnings (-2.58%, session unspecified). Diamondback price path: StockStory snippet 2026-11-03 and Trefis 2026-11-05. Both are proxies, not OXY numbers.

findings.finding: Principal debt was $11.8B at Q2 with $4.2B unrestricted cash, CFFO of $4.6B and FCF of $3.0B in Q2, and the stated next milestone is $10B. Q3 cash flow at $86 WTI likely brings principal debt to about $10B. The company's own slide lists 'opportunistic share repurchases' and 'ongoing principal and net debt reduction' as the subsequent opportunities, so a capital-return update at this print is possible. Against it, the CFO said buybacks are a lower priority until the Berkshire preferred is reduced (redemption from August 2029).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print that announced accelerated paydown and an 8% dividend raise closed +4.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: No Q3 debt figure has been published. If the market expected a buyback at the milestone, previews would quote one; the Aug 7 coverage frames buybacks as low priority. Sized small because of that caveat.
findings.independence: https://boereport.com/2026/08/07/occidental-sees-flat-spending-output-in-2027-keeps-focus-on-debt-reduction/amp/ (CFO: buybacks lower priority, $10B is the immediate priority) partly argues against the upside.

findings.finding: OXY's only crude hedge, two-way collars on 100 Mbbl/d with a $75.89 ceiling, runs March to December 2026 and cost $94M in Q3. Nothing is hedged beyond 2026, so 2027 cash flow carries full exposure to the ~$94-100 strip quoted in early November.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public on slide 22, so mostly priced. It matters only if management frames 2027 cash flow at strip.
findings.independence: The Q3 collar loss of $94M in the 8-K is consistent with the ceiling.
